concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers taken modulo m, with a mod b the remainder of a on division by b.

concepts.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
concepts.gloss: The gcd of two integers is their largest common divisor, and they are coprime when it equals 1.

concepts.name: Prime numbers
concepts.gloss: Integers greater than 1 with no divisors other than 1 and themselves, and every integer factors uniquely into them.

concepts.name: Floor and ceiling functions
concepts.gloss: The floor and ceiling of x are the nearest integers at or below and at or above x.

concepts.name: Binary logarithm
concepts.gloss: lg n is the base-2 logarithm, the number of bits needed to write n.

concepts.name: Binary representation and bit strings
concepts.gloss: Writing nonnegative integers in base 2, and dyadic rationals as integers divided by powers of two.

concepts.name: Exclusive or
concepts.gloss: The bitwise operation that is 1 when exactly one input bit is 1, equal to addition mod 2.

concepts.name: Matrices and linear maps
concepts.gloss: Linear maps between vector spaces represented by matrices, with composition as matrix multiplication and inverses for invertible ones.

concepts.name: Permutations
concepts.gloss: A bijective rearrangement of a finite list of positions.

concepts.name: Subspaces, dimension and rank
concepts.gloss: Linear subspaces of a vector space, their dimension, and the rank of a matrix as the dimension of its image.

concepts.name: Cyclic groups and rings
concepts.gloss: The integers mod m under addition and multiplication, and the basic notion of a ring with addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Cartesian products and tuples
concepts.gloss: Ordered tuples of elements from several sets, used to index multidimensional arrays.

concepts.name: Subsets and combinatorial counting
concepts.gloss: Counting and indexing subsets of a fixed size from a finite set.

concepts.name: Recurrences and geometric series
concepts.gloss: Solving recursive cost relations by unrolling levels and summing a geometric series.

concepts.name: Inequalities and error bounds
concepts.gloss: Bounding sums and products of quantities by absolute value and the triangle inequality.

concepts.name: Gaussian integers
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers a+bi with integer a and b, closed under addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Exponents and powers
concepts.gloss: Powers such as 2^k and x^c, and manipulating real exponents like (lg n)^(1-kappa).

concepts.name: Sorting and scanning arrays
concepts.gloss: Standard sorting and sequential traversal of lists of records.

concepts.name: Schoolbook multiplication
concepts.gloss: The standard digit-by-digit multiplication method taking quadratic time.

concepts.name: Fast Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The divide-and-conquer algorithm computing a length-N discrete Fourier transform in O(N log N) operations.

background.summary: An undergraduate computer scientist who has taken discrete mathematics, linear algebra, algorithms and introductory theory of computation. They know asymptotic notation, divide-and-conquer recurrences, basic number theory (divisibility, gcd, modular arithmetic, primes, Chinese remainder theorem statement), matrices and linear maps, complex numbers and roots of unity, and simple multitape Turing machines. They have not studied the FFT-based multiplication literature in depth, Nussbaumer or Bluestein transforms, fine tape-machine permutation tricks, or finite-ring and numerical-error analysis beyond basics.
